identity.name: Polyperchon's regency
alt_names: Party of the kings (Polyperchon and Olympias)

land.text: Macedon and Thessaly, the regent's seat of government in 319-317

predecessors.note: Not a secession: Polyperchon was the lawful regent ('In 319 BC, shortly before his death, the aging Antipater appointed Polyperchon as regent') and Cassander the rebel; but Cliopatria keeps the empire's colour with Cassander, so this dossier is typed rebel (rule 5 hatch over the Macedonian colour) for the faction that lost.

land.text: Macedon, held by Cassander after Pydna fell 'in the spring of 316'

successors.note: Cassander 'declared himself Regent in 317 BC' and held Macedon from 316.

land.text: Polyperchon's Peloponnesian cities, taken by Demetrius in 303: 'Demetrius Poliorcetes launched a campaign in Greece and quickly reversed many of Polyperchon's gains'

successors.note: Polyperchon disappears from the record after 303/302.

capitals.name: Pella
capitals.note: The regent governed from the Macedonian court with the kings Philip III and Alexander IV until Cassander's return; the page names no city, Pella is the capital of the kingdom (confidence 2). After 316 his seat in the Peloponnese is unknown (Corinth and Sicyon were held by his son Alexander and then Cratesipolis, not on the pages opened).

rulers.name: Polyperchon
rulers.note: Regent of the kings 319-317/316; 'strategos' of the Peloponnese under Cassander from 309. His son Alexander was 'appointed strategos' by 314 (killed that year).

correction.text: Macedon and Thessaly, the regency's area of control, hatched over the Macedonian colour (rule 5); Epirus is removed, being Aeacides's kingdom (dossier kingdom-of-epirus), an ally and not Polyperchon's land

keyframe_review.note: 69.9 k km2, bbox 19.3-24.3 E, 39.7-42.7 N: Upper Macedonia, Pelagonia and Epirus, sitting inside Cliopatria's 4.8 M km2 'Macedonian Empire' shape of the same years. Start a year earlier (319, the appointment) and end in spring 316, when 'the city [Pydna] fell' and Olympias was killed; Polyperchon then 'was driven from Macedon'. Epirus belonged to Aeacides, who 'espoused the cause of Olympias against Cassander, but was dethroned in 313 BC' (Molossians page). In 317 Polyperchon's actual control shrank to the west (Olympias's invasion from Epirus) while Cassander's fleet and army held the coast: a rule 6 blend over Macedon for 317-316.

correction.text: Polyperchon's Peloponnesian cities (Sicyon, Corinth and others held by his son Alexander and his party), approximated as the Peloponnese without Sparta; a hatch over nobody's colour or the Greek city-state colour

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe at confidence 1: Cliopatria drops Polyperchon after 316, but he 'fled to the Peloponnese', 'by 314 BC, his son Alexander had been appointed strategos', 'Cassander excluded Polyperchon from the peace settlement with Antigonus in 311 BC', and in 303 Demetrius 'quickly reversed many of Polyperchon's gains'. Which cities he held in which year is not on the page; the whole peninsula less Sparta is far too generous and a gap-filler should open 'Alexander (son of Polyperchon)' and 'Cratesipolis'. From 309 the hatch becomes a vassal tint under the Macedonian colour (rule 4).

region.text: Macedon and Thessaly, the regent's government

ledger.note: 319: 'In 319 BC, shortly before his death, the aging Antipater appointed Polyperchon as regent' and made Cassander chiliarch; Cassander refused the arrangement and the civil war began. Drawn as a faction over the Macedonian colour from the appointment.

region.text: Macedon, disputed between the regent and Cassander

ledger.note: 317: 'Waging war on Polyperchon, Cassander destroyed his fleet' and 'declared himself Regent in 317 BC'; 'he suffered a major setback at Megalopolis in 317 BC' (Polyperchon page). 'After Olympias' successful move against Philip III later in the year, Cassander besieged her in Pydna.' Rule 6 blend; the macedonian-empire dossier carries the matching pair.
Spring 316: 'When the city fell in the spring of 316, Olympias was killed'. Cassander 'captured and murdered her in 316' (Polyperchon page).
316: Polyperchon driven from Macedon to the Peloponnese after Olympias's death. Cassander 'further cemented his authority by founding Thessalonica, Cassandreia, and rebuilding Thebes'.

region.text: Peloponnesian cities of his party (Sicyon, Corinth and others)

ledger.note: 316-314: the Peloponnesian base. 'By 314 BC, his son Alexander had been appointed strategos (military governor) of the Peloponnese by Cassander', so from 314 the son held the peninsula for Cassander. [Reviewer eu-02-a, 2026-10-18: quote completed from the page.] Confidence 1: the page names no cities; the region is an outer envelope and the counterpart the generic city-state slug. Sparta, never his, is excluded.

309: 'Cassander bribed Polyperchon to kill the boy [Heracles], promising him an alliance and the return of his Macedonian estates'; 'Polyperchon murdered the boy in 309 BC' and was recognised as Cassander's strategos of the Peloponnese. The hatch turns into a vassal tint under the Macedonian colour (rule 4); the macedonian-empire dossier carries the matching pair (309-303).
303: the Peloponnesian cities fall to Demetrius; Polyperchon's command lapses.

303: 'In 303 BC, Demetrius Poliorcetes launched a campaign in Greece and quickly reversed many of Polyperchon's gains' (Sicyon and Corinth among them, per the Demetrius I page's 'In 304-303 he seized cities including Corinth').
303: Polyperchon is 'last heard of' after Demetrius's campaign; his death date is unknown. Cliopatria ends the row in 316.

wars.name: Second War of the Diadochi (Polyperchon and Olympias against Cassander)

zones.text: Olympias's invasion from Epirus and Cassander's reconquest, 317-316

wars.outcome: Cassander's victory: Olympias killed at Pydna (spring 316), Polyperchon driven to the Peloponnese; Aeacides of Epirus, Olympias's ally, 'was dethroned in 313 BC'.
wars.note: Antigonus, Cassander's ally in 319-316, is inside the macedonian-empire shape until 306 and is not a separate belligerent here; Eumenes's eastern war is the me-05 groups' affair.

wars.name: Demetrius's Greek campaign of 303

zones.text: Sicyon, Corinth and the Peloponnesian cities

wars.outcome: Demetrius 'quickly reversed many of Polyperchon's gains' and revived the League of Corinth (302).

certainty.note: A faction, not a bounded state: who held which district of Macedon in 318-316 shifted with the armies.
The Peloponnesian cities are unnamed on the pages; the envelope is an outer limit at confidence 1.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Polyperchon' row (-318..-316, 70 k km2 over Upper Macedonia and Epirus) is kept as a rebel-type faction dossier so that the Macedonian civil war of 319-316 can be hatched (rule 5) over the Macedonian colour, which Cliopatria leaves with Cassander. Changes: start 319 (appointment as regent), the shape trimmed of Epirus (Aeacides's kingdom, dossier epirus), Macedon drawn as a contest for 317-316, and a new Peloponnesian keyframe 315-303 at confidence 1 ending with Demetrius's campaign of 303, after which Polyperchon vanishes. From 309 the Peloponnesian holding is a vassal tint under the macedonian-empire dossier (rule 4), which carries the matching 309-303 pair. The Greek 'freedom decree' of 318 and the sieges of Megalopolis are not territorial. Open: which Peloponnesian cities (Sicyon, Corinth under Alexander's widow Cratesipolis until Ptolemy took them in 308; Messene?) belong to the hatch in which years; the pages opened do not say.
